title: Server Deployment Concepts
summary: Trace the controlled path from receiving a server to monitoring its operation.
objectives: Describe the major stages of a safe server deployment workflow.
Explain why inventory, testing, and documentation are part of deployment.

vocab.def: An identifier assigned to equipment for tracking.
A name used to identify a system on a network.
The controlled process of preparing a system for use.

sections.heading: Deployment is a sequence
sections.body: A conceptual workflow is receive, inspect, inventory, install, cable, configure, test, and monitor. Each stage provides information for the next stage.

sections.heading: Inventory makes systems traceable
sections.body: Synthetic inventory can include an asset tag, serial number, rack position, hostname, status, and purpose. These records should not contain real infrastructure details in class.

sections.heading: Physical work has boundaries
sections.body: Students can trace a deployment with cards or a simulator. Moving heavy equipment, making live connections, and configuring production systems require qualified supervision and authorization.

practice.prompt: Arrange deployment cards in order, then identify one check that belongs before configuration and one check after testing.

quiz.question: Why is inventory part of deployment?
options: It makes equipment and its location traceable
It proves the system is reliable forever
It removes the need for testing
quiz.answer: It makes equipment and its location traceable

lab.objective: Use synthetic asset records to trace a server deployment and identify required checks.

reflectionPrompt: Which deployment stage would you want to understand better, and what evidence would show it was complete?
